style: Say firmly but kindly, like a ship captain giving clear directions
lines: Press a case card in the panel to open your first job.
Press a test in the tray to run it. Then drag each label onto a bottle and press Check labels.
The meter is out for repair. Press an indicator or Conductivity instead.
Some labels are wrong. Move the crossed ones and press Check labels again.
Some bottles still need labels. Pick a label, then press a bottle before Check labels.
Both read 2.4. Press the baking soda buttons a little at a time and watch for the fizz to stop.
Spill rule one. Press Tell the teacher before anything else.
Good. Now press the baking soda buttons and watch the pH graph climb.
Case closed. Every bottle is labeled right.
Press a bottle to fill the beaker, then press any test in the tray.
Pick a label, then press a bottle. Test each bottle before checking labels.
Press a test for each bottle. Your labels need recorded evidence before Check labels can close the case.
Take fresh samples, press Dilute times ten, then press the pH meter for each bottle.
Use your two test records. Pick the explanation that accounts for both amounts and both dilution readings.
Case closed. The same pH concealed very different amounts of acid.
Look at the pH graph after adding extra baking soda. Pick why it is chosen over a strong base.
Case closed. You reported the spill first and tested what happens after the acid is used up.
That explanation does not fit your evidence. Press Fresh sample, then dilute and measure both bottles again.
Press Reset spill, tell the teacher, and rebuild the graph with small steps before trying another explanation.
Press Reset spill and use the smallest soda button near the steep rise. Record both sides before choosing a reason.
Near the steep rise, press the smallest baking soda button. Record both sides before choosing a reason.
A fresh ten milliliter sample is ready. Press a test in the tray.
The bottle is in the beaker. Press a test in the tray.
The acid is used up. Switch bottles to compare, or take a fresh sample to test dilution.
A new shelf has new letter assignments. Test the bottles again before labeling them.
Press Fresh sample before testing or diluting this sample again.
Label selected. Press a bottle to attach it.
Press an indicator or Conductivity to compare this diluted sample.
Press pH meter to measure the diluted sample.
Press Fresh sample before diluting a sample that has reacted.
You passed the endpoint by too much. Press Fresh sample and approach it with smaller steps.
Your soda tests needed different amounts, so equal pH cannot mean equal acid reserves. Press Fresh sample and repeat both dilution readings.
The HCl needed less soda, so it cannot hold the larger acid reserve. Press Fresh sample and repeat both dilution readings.
Your graph rose above seven with extra soda, so bases do not all stop at neutral. Reset spill, tell the teacher, and test again.
The bubbles showed a gas-producing reaction. Reset spill, tell the teacher, and test again.
